transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-10
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Khatri (Redwood SE), Evan Morris (Head of Infra - Redcliff), Lena Ortiz (Security Engineer - Redcliff), Miles Chen (CTO - Redcliff)

Summary:
Redcliff is evaluating whether to run Redwood on Hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private (VPC/on-prem). Main drivers: strict encryption/KMS controls, audit log retention of 7 years, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC with fine-grained roles, and ability to run periodic offline audits. They want an initial pilot on Hosted with encryption at rest managed keys, then a Dedicated benchmark; longer term Private is on the table for regulated workloads.

Topics Covered:
- SOC2 and ISO status and what we can share
- KMS integrations, key residency, HSM options
- SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and role mapping
- RBAC models (tenant/route/model level) and audit logs retention/format
- Data retention and deletion workflows (logs, prompts, KV cache)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for latency, cost, and control
- Next-step benchmarks and docs to share

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'll kick us off. Quick agenda, SOC2/ISO docs, KMS, SSO, RBAC, and then options: hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:18] Evan: cool, yeah we have 30ish minutes to cover the big blockers — for us it's keys and audit trails, retention especially.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): hi all, i'm Priya, i'll go into the se details, how we integrate with customer KMS and how audit logs look. quick note — i might use shorthand, so say if you want me to slow down.
[00:45] Lena: we might interrupt, that's fine. just to set context: Redcliff handles consumer financial data, PII, and some regulated payments flows so retention and chain of custody are critical.
[01:05] Miles: timeline: pilot in Q2, production in Q4 if everything lines up. must have SSO + SCIM and audit log retention policies defined before pilot.
[01:22] Jordan: understood. On soc2, we are in scope and can share our latest attestation — i'll upload a redacted copy. we also maintain an ISO 27001 gap note — i'll add that to the folder. link shared in chat: redwood/security-soc2.pdf (note: placeholder).
[01:45] Evan: can that show encryption key handling? we need explicit language that customer-managed keys are supported for private deployments and a bring-your-own-key model for dedicated.
[02:00] Priya: yes — short answer: for Private you manage keys (BYOK) via your KMS/HSM. for Dedicated we support CMKs via our KMS proxy and you can rotate keys. on Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer key material when required — there are limits w/ hosted providers, we'll detail in the KMS guide.
[02:20] Lena: what's the HSM story — FIPS 140-2 modules?
[02:28] Priya: our private offering can integrate with HSMs that meet FIPS requirements; for hosted we rely on cloud provider HSMs (e.g., AWS KMS with CloudHSM). i need to caveat that for Hosted there are some constraints on key residency depending on region.
[02:42] Miles: so region residency matters — we need EU keys to stay in eu-west.
[02:46] Jordan: yes, we can pin regions for Hosted endpoints and ensure keys reside in EU — will include details.
[03:05] Evan: audit logs — format? do you produce immutable logs with tamper evidence?
[03:12] Priya: logs come in two streams: control plane audit logs (who changed configs, who created model routes, deployments) and runtime request logs (per-request metadata). control plane logs are pushed to customer log sinks (S3, GCS, or SIEM via syslog/kinesis). we also support append-only write to an audit bucket with versioning enabled so you can retain an immutable copy.
[03:40] Lena: what's the retention policy and can we set retention to 7 years?
[03:46] Priya: the platform defaults to 90 days for runtime logs on Hosted, but we provide hooks to stream to your long-term storage; retention in that case is your responsibility. for Dedicated and Private you can configure retention to 7 years by writing to your own archived bucket. we'll document sample lifecycle policies.
[04:10] Evan: ok. how granular are the runtime logs? are prompts stored verbatim? we have to redact PII automatically if stored.
[04:20] Jordan: behavior depends on deployment and customer choice. for Hosted you can opt-in to store request/response payloads; by default we do aggregate tokens for billing and telemetry. for the pilot we can enable request-level logging into your encrypted archive, and we can show how to implement a PII redaction layer before storage.
[04:42] Miles: do you have built-in PII scrubbers or do we need to implement a pre/post processing layer?
[04:50] Priya: we provide a plugins pattern — you can attach a pre-save redaction step. it's not a black box auto-scrubber for Hosted by default, because accuracy matters and we don't want to silently transform user content. for Dedicated/Private customers we often deploy sidecar redaction or use your existing DLP pipeline.
[05:12] Evan: let's talk SSO — we use Okta and OneLogin for different teams. want SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[05:20] Priya: we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user/group provisioning. role mapping is flexible: you can map SAML groups to Redwood roles (admin, developer, auditor, billing) and we can support custom roles at the org or route level. we'll share example metadata.
[05:45] Lena: do you support adaptive access / MFA enforcement via the IdP? we need MFA for all admin-role logins.
[05:52] Jordan: MFA is enforced by the IdP — Redwood honors the assertions. we can also restrict actions using RBAC + conditional policies.
[06:10] Miles: for RBAC we need separation so our SREs can't pull raw prompts unless explicitly allowed. can we audit who accessed raw text?
[06:20] Priya: yes, audit trail includes who accessed which artifacts. we can show example audit entries — timestamp, user, action, route/model id, and request id. redaction status will also be in the record.
[06:40] Evan: token usage / KV cache — how long is cached memory kept? for private prompts we'd like a TTL of 0 for KV cache for certain workflows.
[06:52] Priya: you can configure KV cache TTL per route. default is per-session caching for performance, but we expose route-level configs to disable or set short TTLs; that works for private deployments as well. note: sometimes the transcription says "kay vee cache" which causes confusion but the feature is KV (key-value) cache.
[07:15] Lena: nice. what's the model fallback policy you mentioned earlier? we need predictable degradation if capacity runs out.
[07:22] Jordan: we have routing policies: prefer low-latency region, then cost-pref, then fallback to a smaller quantized variant; we can also pin dedicated capacity for mission-critical routes so there is no fallback. we'll go over policy examples in the doc.
[07:45] Miles: network access — do you offer private endpoints for hosted or only for Private/Dedicated?
[07:52] Priya: Hosted supports regional private endpoints with VPC peering in some regions (beta), Dedicated offers customer-dedicated VPC peering and Private is fully in your VPC/on-prem. specifics depend on the package.
[08:10] Evan: let's surface an example threat scenario: an insider pulls prompts. what's mitigation?
[08:18] Priya: mitigation is multi-layer: RBAC least privilege, immutable audit logs with alerting, and optional encryption of stored prompts with customer keys. for real-time prevention you can route request content through DLP before storage.
[08:40] Lena: on compliance evidence — will Redwood provide logs for audits and how are they delivered?
[08:46] Jordan: yes, we can provide logs as snapshots to your SOC team via secure export; for Dedicated/Private customers we frequently give access to the control plane audit logs and a read-only view into event history. we'll include a sample extract format (CSV + raw gzipped JSON).
[09:15] Evan: are there API rate limits on log retrieval for audits? some audit tools pull a lot.
[09:22] Priya: we recommend pushing logs to your storage to avoid heavy pulls. for ad-hoc retrieval we throttle and can open a support ticket for bulk export.
[09:45] Miles: encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS, but at rest do you support customer key rotation without downtime?
[09:55] Priya: yes for Dedicated/Private we support key rotation with minimal disruption; we use envelope encryption so new data can be encrypted with the new key while old data can be rewrapped. for Hosted we coordinate rotations with underlying cloud provider constraints.
[10:20] Evan: how about backups and disaster recovery — what RTO/RPOs?
[10:28] Jordan: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed RTO/RPO per contract; Hosted defaults are documented (RTO ~4 hrs for control plane incidents), but for mission-critical we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity. we'll include SLOs in the doc.
[10:55] Lena: curious about penetration tests and vuln disclosures — do you do third-party appsec pen tests and will we get an executive summary?
[11:02] Jordan: yes, annual third-party pentests; we provide exec summaries and remediation timelines, redacted reports can be shared after an NDA.
[11:25] Evan: any regulatory frameworks you specifically support? we have EU financial regs and some UK-specific guidance.
[11:32] Priya: we have customers in EU finance; we can map Redwood controls to common frameworks — SOC2, ISO 27001, and we'll provide a control mapping to show coverage for privacy and financial regs.
[11:50] Miles: is there an on-prem appliance or do you only do VPC/private control plane?
[11:58] Priya: we have a Private deployment that can be fully on-prem; it's a packaged deployment with a private control plane and optional air-gapped mode for very regulated customers. installation requires collaboration with our infra team — estimate a 6–12 week project depending on environment.
[12:22] Evan: cost delta between Dedicated and Private? not exact numbers but relative magnitude.
[12:28] Jordan: Dedicated has lower up-front integration cost and faster time to production; Private has higher initial integration and runbook overhead but gives maximal control and can be cost-neutral for large steady workloads due to customer infra amortization. we'll provide cost model examples.
[12:50] Lena: logging format again — do you include user identifiers hashed or plain? we prefer hashed PII fields with salt we control.
[12:58] Priya: we can hash or pseudonymize fields before export. the export tooling includes a transform hook so you can run a hashing function (with your salt) before logs land in the archive.
[13:18] Evan: audit retention in control plane — do you retain configuration change history longer than runtime logs?
[13:25] Priya: control plane changes we retain for 1 year in the default, but again you can stream the control plane audit to your archive for long-term retention.
[13:40] Jordan: quick interjection — i'll capture these specifics and make a short FAQ doc so your auditors can review.
[13:48] Miles: sweet.
[14:00] Evan: any blockers with SCIM provisioning for nested groups? we have nested groups that map to team roles.
[14:07] Priya: SCIM v2 supports group nesting in our idp connector; we'll share a sample mapping. watch out for limit in some idps that flatten groups.
[14:30] Lena: logs of who viewed redacted vs raw content — can that be separate events?
[14:35] Priya: yes, we annotate events with access level; view_raw_content:event vs view_redacted:event. it's included in the schema.
[14:55] Evan: for the pilot, we want hosted but with customer-controlled key wrapping and logs streamed to our GCS bucket. is that a typical pattern?
[15:04] Jordan: yes that's a common hybrid for proofs. we'll show the KMS proxy pattern in docs.
[15:22] Miles: about SLA and uptime — if we go Dedicated, can we get latency SLOs as low as 25ms p95 for a specific model?
[15:30] Priya: depends on model size and hardware; we can target low p95s with dedicated GPU pools and tuning. we'll propose hardware shapes and expected p95 in the benchmark plan.
[16:00] Evan: benchmarks — we need to run with our prompt distribution and token lengths; is that something Redwood will run?
[16:08] Jordan: yes, we'll run a dedicated benchmark if you provide traces. Priya will coordinate.
[16:25] Lena: last compliance question — can you provide evidence for segregation of duties in your ops team?
[16:33] Jordan: yes, we'll produce a control mapping showing role separation and access policies; some items might be redacted but the mapping will be explicit.
[16:50] Miles: ok good.
[17:05] Evan: any known limitations in Hosted around synchronous streaming or function calling inside a VPC?
[17:12] Priya: streaming works, but if you require private network streaming, that usually falls to Dedicated/Private for predictable throughput. Hosted private endpoints are beta in some regions.
[17:38] Jordan: quick recap idea — pilot: Hosted with KMS envelope + logs to GCS; run benchmark with sample traces; provide SOC2/ISO docs; schedule deep-dive on Dedicated if benchmarks need it. Thoughts?
[17:55] Lena: that sounds right. one ask: can you share a short runbook of incident response steps for a suspected key compromise?
[18:02] Priya: yes — we'll include an incident playbook that covers key rotation, revocation, and rewrap steps and responsibilities.
[18:20] Evan: also need a contact for urgent compliance questions — SOC contact?
[18:25] Jordan: that's me for now; i'll route to security and se as needed.
[18:40] Miles: timeline recap — jordan to send docs mid-week, priya to send KMS/SCIM samples, evan to gather traces. schedule benchmark week of 3/22.
[19:00] Jordan: perfect. any final quick questions?
[19:05] Lena: are there log schemas you can share now?
[19:10] Priya: yes i'll attach sample audit CSV + json schema, will send with the KMS doc.
[19:25] Evan: thanks all.
[19:30] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts.
